deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether Terraform can destroy the resource. A policy should require destruction protection (for example, PREVENT) to reduce accidental or malicious deletion of critical infrastructure.

description.description: Optional. A human-readable description of the resource.
description.rationale: Human-readable description used for documentation only. It does not affect the security posture of the resource.

labels.description:
Optional. Set of labels associated with the WasmPlugin resource.

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Metadata used for organization and resource management. Labels do not affect security behaviour.

location.description: The location of the traffic extension
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

main_version_id.description: The ID of the WasmPluginVersion resource that is the currently serving one. The version referred to must be a child of this WasmPlugin resource and should be listed in the "versions" field.
main_version_id.rationale: References the plugin version that is currently active. It is a reference to another resource version, and platform policy should not dictate which version a team deploys.

name.description: Identifier. Name of the WasmPlugin resource.
name.rationale: Resource identifier only. Platform policy should not constrain resource names.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Identifies the Google Cloud project containing the resource. Platform policy should not constrain project identifiers.

log_config.description:
Optional. Specifies the logging options for the activity performed by this plugin. If logging is enabled, plugin logs are exported to Cloud Logging.
Note that the settings relate to the logs generated by using logging statements in your Wasm code.

log_config.enable.description: Optional. Specifies whether to enable logging for activity by this plugin.
log_config.enable.rationale: Controls whether plugin activity is logged. A policy should require logging to be enabled to support monitoring, auditing and incident investigation.

log_config.min_log_level.description:
Non-empty default. Specificies the lowest level of the plugin logs that are exported to Cloud Logging. This setting relates to the logs generated by using logging statements in your Wasm code.
This field is can be set only if logging is enabled for the plugin.
If the field is not provided when logging is enabled, it is set to INFO by default. Possible values: ["LOG_LEVEL_UNSPECIFIED", "TRACE", "DEBUG", "INFO", "WARN", "ERROR", "CRITICAL"]
log_config.min_log_level.rationale: Controls the minimum severity of exported logs. A policy should require a level that captures security-relevant events and should not disable meaningful logging.

log_config.sample_rate.description:
Non-empty default. Configures the sampling rate of activity logs, where 1.0 means all logged activity is reported and 0.0 means no activity is reported.
A floating point value between 0.0 and 1.0 indicates that a percentage of log messages is stored.
The default value when logging is enabled is 1.0. The value of the field must be between 0 and 1 (inclusive).
This field can be specified only if logging is enabled for this plugin.
log_config.sample_rate.rationale: Controls how much plugin activity is logged. A policy should require an adequate sampling rate (for example, greater than zero) so security events are available for auditing.

versions.description: All versions of this WasmPlugin resource in the key-value format. The key is the resource ID, and the value is the VersionDetails object.

versions.description.description: Optional. A human-readable description of the resource.
versions.description.rationale: Human-readable description for the plugin version. It is documentation only and has no security impact.

versions.image_uri.description:
Optional. URI of the container image containing the plugin, stored in the Artifact Registry. When a new WasmPluginVersion resource is created, the digest of the container image is saved in the imageDigest field.
When downloading an image, the digest value is used instead of an image tag.
versions.image_uri.rationale: References the container image stored in Artifact Registry. It is a reference to another resource, and platform policy should not constrain which image repository or URI is used.

versions.labels.description: Optional. Set of labels associated with the WasmPlugin resource.
versions.labels.rationale: Metadata used for organization and resource management. Labels do not affect security behaviour.

versions.plugin_config_data.description:
A base64-encoded string containing the configuration for the plugin. The configuration is provided to the plugin at runtime through the ON_CONFIGURE callback.
When a new WasmPluginVersion resource is created, the digest of the contents is saved in the pluginConfigDigest field.
Conflics with pluginConfigUri.
versions.plugin_config_data.rationale: Contains a Base64-encoded plugin configuration. This is a free-form configuration blob that cannot be meaningfully constrained by a generic platform security policy.

versions.plugin_config_uri.description:
URI of the plugin configuration stored in the Artifact Registry. The configuration is provided to the plugin at runtime through the ON_CONFIGURE callback.
The container image must contain only a single file with the name plugin.config.
When a new WasmPluginVersion resource is created, the digest of the container image is saved in the pluginConfigDigest field.
Conflics with pluginConfigData.
versions.plugin_config_uri.rationale: References plugin configuration stored in Artifact Registry. It is a reference to another resource, and platform policy should not dictate which configuration artifact is used.

versions.version_name.description: The identifier for this object. Format specified above.
versions.version_name.rationale: Identifier for the plugin version. Platform policy should not constrain resource names or version identifiers.
